findings.title: Cleanup debug logs left at Error level with full ID lists
findings.body: CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags call r.log.Error on every batch (lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, and 579), including the successful path where err is nil. Each line dumps the full ids slice and the SQL condition. With a configured batch size in the tens of thousands this writes enormous error-level log records on every cleanup cycle even when nothing is wrong, flooding logs and adding allocation/IO cost to the job the PR is trying to make safer. These should be removed or reduced to debug without the ID list.

findings.title: Cleanup ticker shortened from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: Run now starts the background cleanup ticker at 1 minute instead of 10. Nothing in the PR description or the deadlock fix requires this, and it looks like leftover debugging next to the new Error logs. clean() uses a 9-minute timeout and runs synchronously, while time.Ticker buffers one tick, so a job longer than a minute will be re-entered immediately and the whole cleanup suite (annotations, snapshots, dashboard versions, images, invites, short URLs, query history) can run nearly continuously. That multiplies database load and can recreate the write contention this change is meant to avoid.

findings.title: SQLite ID list built with quadratic string concatenation
findings.body: When the SQLite fallback inlines IDs because AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize exceeds 999, deleteByIDs grows the IN-list with fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v) on every element. That copies the whole string each iteration. The new integration test exercises this path with a batch of 32767, so a single DELETE statement build is quadratic in the batch size and can stall the cleanup goroutine for a large annotation table. Build the list with strings.Builder or strings.Join instead.
